content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P0 triggered for eu-west-2: multiple customer 5xx errors, high error-rate on inference-hosts behind nat-gw-eu2-01
Sam Patel: I got the page, jumping on it.
Priya Nair: Confirming errors from telemetry: outbound requests to external token service timing out ~100% from AZ2 private subnets (subnet-az2-priv-03).
Marta Gomez: I'm on the bastion. Quick check: can curl out?
Marta Gomez: `curl -v https://api.tokenizer.example` -> hangs, then TLS handshake timeout.
Sam Patel: AWS Console shows NAT gateway nat-gw-eu2-01 with status "available" but CloudWatch NAT packetsDropped metric spiked.
Priya Nair: Also seeing a sudden Route Table change event in config history around 3141592600. Possible automated change?
Alice (Support): Customers reporting elevated 502s for hosted-api in eu-west-2. Ticket heap increasing.
Kevin Liu: I'm taking incident commander. Assigning roles: Kevin IC, Sam networking lead, Priya analysis, Marta mitigation. Handoff in 2m.
incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incidents.3141592653. PagerDuty escalation notified.
Sam Patel: On the route table for priv-subnet-az2-03 I see an extra 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing to a VPC peering attachment (pcx-0abc) that goes to another account — that looks wrong (split-horizon leak).
Priya Nair: Why would a peering target become preferred for 0.0.0.0/0? Route priority/regeneration bug? I see a Terraform apply around that time by infra-deploy-bot: `apply --target=aws_vpc_peering_connection.route-leak`
Marta Gomez: Quick mitigation: remove the peered route or replace to nat-gw. I can revert the route in RT rtb-0a1b2c.
Sam Patel: Hold on before removing: need to check whether the peering has propagated a higher priority route via propagated routes. If we remove incorrectly we might break internal cross-account traffic.
Kevin Liu: We need a fast fallback to restore customer egress. Plan: create a new explicit 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-eu2-01 route with higher precedence (non-propagated local route) and add a NACL temporary allow for ephemeral ports. Marta, can you create the route?
Marta Gomez: Creating route now. CLI:```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-gw-0d4e5f```
Marta Gomez: Route replace returned success.
Priya Nair: Re-testing from bastion: `curl -I https://api.tokenizer.example` -> 200 OK now. :thumbsup:
Alice (Support): Support dashboard shows a drop in 5xx volume for hosted-api — thanks team. Customers being notified.
Sam Patel: Need to check root cause: why did the peering route appear as global default. Pulling CloudTrail for route updates.
Kevin Liu: Also check automation runs: terraform state & apply logs. Add infra-deploy-bot to thread.
incident-bot: Added label: "customer-impact: partial"; impact: "hosted-api eu-west-2 degraded for ~6m".
Priya Nair: CloudTrail shows `ModifyRoute` from user: infra-deploy-bot assumed-role:infra-automation at 3141592598. Terraform plan included a security fix but unintentionally targeted rtb-0a1b2c due to a variable interpolation bug.
Sam Patel: So not an upstream AWS failure, that explains the split-horizon leak. Need postmortem on deploy gating.
Marta Gomez: I'm applying a guard: tag rtb-0a1b2c with `do-not-modify=true` and adding a quick policy to infra automation to skip route-tables with that tag. Pushing change to infra repo.
Kevin Liu: Handoff: I'm stepping out in 20m, Sam will be primary until next shift. Sam, confirm you'll follow through on remediation & postmortem doc.
Sam Patel: Confirming. I'll own the PM and roll forward the tag-based guard and a canary test for route changes.
Alice (Support): Drafting customer-facing note. ETA for a more detailed update ~30m.
Priya Nair: Final check: NAT metrics look normal, no additional spikes in packetsDropped. We'll keep monitoring for 30m then declare mitigated.
incident-bot: Status changed to: mitigated (customer-impact: partial) by Kevin Liu at 3141592899. Incident timeline: detection 3141592560 -> mitigation 3141592678 -> declared mitigated 3141592899.
Kevin Liu: Closing notes: root cause = automation bug in infra-deploy targeting wrong RTB leading to default route to peering; impact = 6m of outbound egress failures for AZ2; mitigation = replace-route to NAT gateway + tag-based guard + policy update + postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: Priya (postmortem), Marta (policy change), Sam (canary tests), Alice (customer comms). Thanks everyone. :bow:
